title: Birches in October
note: A birch grove in autumn, late in the day: oil on toned canvas, thin to thick, the trunks laid with a knife and the leaves in thick dabs. Written by paintings/birches.gen.mjs.

rub.note: colour thinned with turpentine and scrubbed in

paint.note: paint as it comes from the tube

dark.note: a dark that keeps its shine

impasto.note: thick clean paint that does not sink into what is under it

slab.note: a short pull of the knife

steps.name: Ground
steps.note: Burnt sienna rubbed thinly over the toned canvas, so that no bare canvas shows and the gold has something warm under it.

steps.name: Sky
steps.note: Pale blue above, warm cream toward the wood: broad strokes, worked into each other while wet.

steps.name: Far wood
steps.note: The trees behind: violet-grey and dull gold, upright touches, kept soft.

steps.name: Floor of the wood
steps.note: Fallen leaves: ochre, gold and rust in strokes that lie flat and grow larger toward us.

steps.name: Shadows
steps.note: The trunks throw long violet shadows across the leaves; between them the low sun lies in bands.

steps.name: Leaves behind
steps.note: The mass of the foliage: dull gold and rust first, so that the bright leaves have something to shine against.

steps.name: Trunks
steps.note: White bark with the knife on the side of the sun, grey-violet in the shade; then the black bands, the scars and the branches.

steps.name: Leaves
steps.note: Thick dabs of yellow, laid last and left alone. A few are falling.

steps.name: Last touches
steps.note: A few dry grasses and bright leaves at our feet.
